verified.resolved_title: Prevalence of Intimate Partner Violence in Thailand
verified.note: Sample n=2,462 married/cohabiting women 20-59, four regions of Thailand, WHO multi-country instrument -- all confirmed. Controlling-behaviour range '4.6% to 29.3%' confirmed verbatim. BUT the abstract states lifetime psychological/physical/sexual IPV prevalence as '15%' ('1 in 6'), not the more precise '15.4%' the draft cites -- that decimal is not supported by the abstract text (may be in a table/full text not visible here). Use '~15%' or verify 15.4% against the full-text table before keeping the precise figure. National (4-region) survey, not southern-border-specific -- fine as general Thailand background, not deep-south-specific evidence.

verified.resolved_title: Intimate partner violence and factors associated with sexually transmitted infections among Thai women attending gynecology clinics
verified.note: n=400 confirmed ('Among 400 participants'); 21% past-year IPV confirmed ('84 (21%) had ever experienced ... in the past year'); IPV-STI association OR 2.65 (95% CI 1.11-6.28) confirmed verbatim. Setting is two gynecology clinics at a university hospital in Bangkok -- NOT the southern border provinces; draft claim correctly states 'Bangkok university gynaecology clinic', so population framing is accurate as written.

verified.resolved_title: Intimate partner violence among pregnant Thai women
verified.note: n=475 pregnant Thai women confirmed; 13.1% ever abused and 4.8% physical abuse during pregnancy confirmed verbatim; abused women reported lower positive health practices and higher depressive symptoms, matching claim. Abstract does not name a specific province/region (general 'pregnant Thai women') -- not southern-border-specific; draft does not claim it is, so no mismatch, but it should not be cited as deep-south evidence.

verified.resolved_title: Perceptions of Screening Women for Intimate Partner Violence Among Health Care Providers in Thailand
verified.note: n=32 health care providers (30 nurses, 2 social workers) in secondary/tertiary hospitals confirmed exactly; barriers (cultural norms, lack of training) and value-of-screening themes confirmed. HOWEVER the abstract specifies the hospitals are in NORTHEAST Thailand, not the southern border provinces -- the draft's claim omits region, which is technically not false but should not be used to characterize deep-south-specific provider attitudes without noting the actual (northeast) setting.

verified.resolved_title: A cross-sectional study on factors influencing adolescent depression in the civil-conflict areas of Thailand
verified.note: n=387 confirmed (179 males + 208 females = 387); 7.2% at risk of depression on Thai CES-D cut-off confirmed verbatim; dysfunctional family aOR 3.20 (95% CI 1.18-8.15) for depression confirmed; PTSD aOR 32.74 (95% CI 4.08-267.76) for depression confirmed, and CI is indeed very wide as claimed. Note the draft's phrasing 'family dysfunction aOR ~3.2 depression, ~32.7 PTSD' is shorthand for two separate predictors of the same depression outcome (family dysfunction and PTSD), not two different outcomes -- accurate but could be phrased more clearly. Setting: three southernmost provinces (Yala/Pattani/Narathiwat), adolescents 13-17, 2021 household survey -- correct.

overall_note: 13 of 18 record IDs resolve to real, PubMed-indexed articles (note two IDs point to the same HSRI report, so this is 16 distinct sources: 11 journal-article PMIDs + 1 duplicate-counted HSRI report + 4 TCI-only journal items). All four DOI-cited items ARE PubMed-indexed: Chuemchit 2018 (PMID 29904232, J Fam Violence), Nursing for Women's Health 2024 (PMID 39536796), Conflict and Health 2026 (PMID 41540416), and BMC Public Health 2026 (PMID 41872869) -- despite the 2026 publication years these are real, currently-indexed PubMed/MEDLINE records (this workspace's clock reads 2026-09-02, so 2026 pub dates are plausible, not evidence of fabrication; each was independently confirmed via efetch with matching title/author/journal/DOI). Of the 11 numeric PMID/DOI claims checked against abstracts, 9 are fully supported verbatim (KEEP) and 2 need correction (FIX): (1) Chuemchit's cited '15.4%' lifetime IPV prevalence is not in the abstract, which states '15%' ('1 in 6') -- the controlling-behaviour range 4.6-29.3% and n=2,462 are exact; (2) the Conflict and Health 2026 paper's specific SRQ>=8 prevalence figures (9.5% overall, 12.8% women, 5.1% men) do not appear anywhere in its abstract even though the qualitative findings (parental absence, travel worry, father absence, male-protective religiosity) all check out -- these percentages must be verified against the full-text results table before being kept, or dropped/hedged if unverifiable. The Nursing for Women's Health 2024 study, while numerically accurate (n=32), is set in NORTHEAST Thailand, not the southern border provinces, and should not be cited as deep-south-specific evidence. All 5 CONTEXT-ONLY items (TCI:Nubuu-211693, HSRI:11228/4378 [cited twice], TCI:JHS-14901, TCI:AMS-66346, TCI:JHS-15067) were confirmed absent from PubMed via title/keyword esearch as expected, and per the repo's PubMed-only literature-review rule these are correctly excluded from the medical-claims evidence base -- usable only as background/context with explicit non-PubMed labeling, never as citations for the numeric medical claims. No item was dropped outright: every PubMed-resolvable citation was genuine and none showed evidence of fabrication or citation mismatch.
